node.customTimeInstruction: All levels. 15 and under accompanied by adult
node.descriptionText:
Instructions

The Dance Studio is located on the lower level of Yale Schwarzman Center, 168 Grove Street, New Haven, CT 06511.

SPECIAL 2PM CLASS TIME

Free and open to the public with registration.
We welcome people ages 15 and under when accompanied by an adult.
If you need technical assistance with registration or require accessible accommodations contact ysc.info@yale.edu.

Doors open at 1:30Pm.

EveryBody Dances @ Yale Schwarzman Center brings local and visiting dance artists to our Dance Studio to teach masterclasses in jazz, hip hop, salsa, modern, contemporary, precision dance and more! All community members are welcome. This week's class will be led by Bijayini Satpathy. 

Satpathy will teach a workshop in the unique art of Abhinaya or the language of Expressional Dance.  This class encompasses learning of 9 basic emotions, the language of hand gestures and their application. The participants will then learn to translate ideas, imagination and stories through facial expressions and gestural language.

Clothing recommendations: 

Indian style Kurta and Salwar or long Yoga pants and T-shirts are recommended. 

Shorts and skirts are not allowed. 

Dancers will need to move on bare feet.

node.name: Sunday Trivia Nights at Bobbi’s
node.descriptionText:
Trivia at Bobbi’s runs about 90 minutes and is played over five rounds. The game features a slideshow format with image-based and puzzle categories, making it engaging, easy to follow, and accessible for players with hearing difficulties.

Questions span history, science, music, film, television, geography, and more, creating a well-rounded game that appeals to players of all experience levels and interests.

A strong emphasis is placed on teamwork, with categories designed to encourage group thinking and collaboration. Bobbi’s puzzle rounds are especially popular, known for their creativity and memorable “A-ha!” moments.

Trivia at Bobbi’s is always free to play, with prizes and bragging rights for the top-scoring teams. All are welcome!

node.name: From Planet to Parenthood: The Hidden Mental Health Costs of a Changing Climate
node.descriptionText:
Our planet is changing, and so are the challenges facing maternal mental health. Rising pollution, resource scarcity, and climate change are placing growing pressures on the mental well-being of pregnant and postpartum women. Yet their needs remain largely overlooked, despite evidence suggesting that climate-related stressors can double the incidence of common perinatal mental disorders, from 20% to as high as 40%.

Join UNFPA Asia-Pacific Regional Office, the Planetary Health Alliance, and Jhpiego for a webinar exploring perinatal mental health through a Planetary Health lens. During this webinar, we will explore how planetary changes are affecting women, midwives, and maternity services, and present findings from UNFPA Asia-Pacific's scoping review on climate and perinatal mental health, developed in partnership with Jhpiego. We’ll finish by exploring practical steps Universities and thought leaders can take to address this issue.

node.name: Volunteer with Sunrise Cafe!
node.descriptionText:
Start your morning off on a great note! Join Dwight Hall Monday and Wednesday mornings to volunteer at Sunrise Cafe. Sunrise Cafe is an early morning soup kitchen that serves New Haven's homeless and food-insecure every weekday from 6:30 A.M. to 8:30 A.M. The service site is located at 57 Olive St., just a 15 minute walk from Phelps Gate. Volunteers will meet in front of Phelps Gate at 6:00am, walk together to Sunrise Cafe, and will return to campus by 9:00am.

To sign up, please request to join DWIGHT HALL VOLUNTEER CORPS, and we will approve your request as soon as possible.

Sunrise Cafe has been serving breakfast without charge to New Haven's homeless and hungry since 2015. Each weekday morning, the Cafe welcomes guests to the undercroft of St. Paul and St. James, near Wooster Square and three blocks south of the New Haven Green with white tablecloths, flowers and a rotating menu of fresh, warm, nutritious home-cooked food. Your generosity opens our doors.

Cheerful volunteers take each order individually, deliver the breakfast to our guest and help our paid chefs in the kitchen. Staff and volunteers ensure every guest is warmly welcomed.

Sunrise Cafe is uniquely welcoming and secure, based on trust and mutual respect, and the rapport built between the volunteer servers and our guests. With a warm welcome and just two rules – no drugs on the premises and no arguments – Sunrise has become a community center for the homeless, a place to come every weekday morning and gather with friends.

Hungry friends come for the home-cooked, nourishing breakfast and stay for simple medical services offered by the Cornell Scott Health Center and access to support from social services to find housing.

Sunrise provides a unique opportunity to bridge New Haven's inequalities that separate us from one another. Volunteers come once and become regulars. Guests and volunteers become friends and greet one another on the street.

If you have any questions, email maryann.dang@yale.edu

node.name: Monday Mindfulness Meditation
node.descriptionText:
Free afternoon group meditation held on Zoom sponsored by Being Well at Yale (Employee Well-being).  Sessions are held during the academic year September through mid-December and mid-January through end of May. 

Taking a break during the workday to pause and practice mindfulness has been shown to be beneficial for enhancing executive function, increasing emotional regulation, and reducing cortisol levels. Meditations are a mix of guided and silent. Time for reflections and optional sharing is also included at the conclusion of the practice. 

Beginners welcome! No experience necessary. No special equipment required. Open to Yale University employees. 

Sessions are led by Danielle Casioppo, Education Specialist and Certified Mindfulness-Based Strengths Practice instructor with Being Well at Yale / Employee Well-being. 

To join please send a request to beingwell@yale.edu and specify your Yale affiliation. You will then be added to the Yale meditation email list serve. The Zoom link to join the sessions is included in the weekly reminder emails.

node.name: Thanksgiving at Home 2026 (Participant Sign-Up)
node.descriptionText:
[Nov 17 Important Note]
OISS will try our very best to pair you up with a host this Thanksgiving. But please note that this Yale Connect RSVP is not a guarantee for a program placement. OISS will be reaching out shortly after your RSVP to coordinate logistics and placements.

Are you an international student or scholar who would like to spend this Thanksgiving with a host family? Do you plan to stay in town for the last week of November and but don't want to miss out on this unique American tradition? OISS got something for you!

Thanksgiving at Home is one of our favorite traditions, and a great opportunity to experience an American holiday with a local family. Our hosts come from a variety of backgrounds in the Yale community, each with their own set of family traditions.

We do our best to place as many students and scholars as possible, but we cannot guarantee your space until you have been matched with a host, and until you confirm your attendance with us (details to follow).

By registering for this program, you must be available all day on Thursday, November 26th to be eligible to be placed with a family. Please only sign-up if you are positive that you will be here and can attend. You will be contacted no later than November 19th to confirm that you have been matched with a host family, and further details will be shared at that time.

PLEASE READ BEFORE REGISTERING:
- This program is only open to Yale international students and scholars, and if possible, and their spouses and children.
- While we do our best to place friends together, we cannot guarantee that it is possible.
- Please note that every individual must register separately for the program. If you are a family, please register everyone individually (including children). In the registration there will be a place for you to indicate who you would like to be placed with (for friends and family), and the OISS will be in touch for arrangement; again, we try our best but that's not always possible.
- While this program is free, some of our hosts live outside of New Haven and might require you to take a train or share an Uber/Lyft to get to their house. When registering, please keep in mind there might be a cost associated with transportation to get to/from your host's home, but we do our best to keep costs minimal.
- We also ask that each family unit or individual participant (whichever applies) bring a dish to share with the host family on the day of event.
- If you are registering with children, please keep in mind that our host families aren't always able to take an entire family for the holiday, but we will do our best to find a place for you.
- If you are registering for this program (Thanksgiving at Home), please refrain from also registering for International Thanksgiving Potluck.

Get ready for some classic Thanksgiving dishes like mashed potatoes and pumpkin pie!
